title: Create a data loader to train a model

cues.en: As I mentioned in the previous video, this and the next several videos are focused on one specific
cues.zh: 如上一支影片所說，這支與接下來幾支，聚焦同一個

cues.en: topic, which is training and embeddings matrix from scratch with real text data.
cues.zh: 主題：用真實文字資料，從零訓練嵌入矩陣。

cues.en: So the purpose of this video is just to create the data set in the format that our PyTorch model will need.
cues.zh: 這支影片，只建立 PyTorch 模型需要的資料格式。

cues.en: We're going to create the deep learning model in the next video and then train it after that.
cues.zh: 下一支影片建立深度學習模型，之後再訓練。

cues.en: Here we are only focused on organizing the data set.
cues.zh: 這裡只專注整理資料集。

cues.en: And in order to create that data set, you're also going to learn about some terms and parameters of training text data.
cues.zh: 建立過程，也會學到文字訓練資料的一些術語與參數。

cues.en: Let's start with some terms.
cues.zh: 先看術語。

cues.en: So these are all terms that I'm going to define over in this space here.
cues.zh: 這些詞，都會在這裡定義，

cues.en: And then I'll show examples with the real sentence up here.
cues.zh: 再用上方真實句子展示例子。

cues.en: And after that I'll explain what we're going to do in the Python demo.
cues.zh: 之後，解釋 Python 示範要做什麼。

cues.en: And by the way some of these terms might already look familiar to you from previous books or courses that you might have studied about deep learning.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，如果讀過其他深度學習書籍或課程，有些詞可能已熟悉。

cues.en: For example, convolutional neural networks and stride.
cues.zh: 例如，卷積神經網路中的 stride。

cues.en: Anyway, you will see that these terms are basically the same thing.
cues.zh: 你會看到，這裡基本上是相同概念。

cues.en: Okay, so to start with we have the inputs and the targets to the model.
cues.zh: 首先，模型的輸入與目標。

cues.en: The input is a token sequence, for example a sentence or a snippet of text.
cues.zh: 輸入是 token 序列，例如句子或文字片段，

cues.en: That's what you feed into the model.
cues.zh: 也就是送進模型的資料。

cues.en: And then the target is just a shifted version of that same sequence.
cues.zh: 目標則是同一序列平移後的版本。

cues.en: In other words, you take exactly the same token input sequence and then shift it by one token.
cues.zh: 換句話說，取完全相同的輸入 token 序列，再平移一個 token。

cues.en: That means that the model is going to predict each subsequent token.
cues.zh: 這表示，模型要預測每個後續 token。

cues.en: I'll show an example of this in a moment, and you'll see more examples when I switch to code.
cues.zh: 稍後看例子，切換到程式後，也會看到更多。

cues.en: But let me first briefly define these other parameters.
cues.zh: 先簡短定義其他參數。

cues.en: So here we have sequence length.
cues.zh: 這是序列長度。

cues.en: This is simply the number of tokens that you feed into the model at a time.
cues.zh: 就是一次送進模型的 token 數。

cues.en: Longer sequences are better because that gives the model a larger context window for using tokens to predict the next token.
cues.zh: 較長序列比較好，因為提供更大上下文視窗，用來預測下一個 token。

cues.en: Next up is stride.
cues.zh: 接著是步幅，stride。

cues.en: Stride is how many tokens between sequences you skip, so each successive sequence that you input to
cues.zh: 步幅，是相鄰序列的起點移動幾個 token；每次送入

cues.en: the model can be generated by skipping one token or several tokens.
cues.zh: 模型的新序列，可以往後移一個或好幾個 token 產生。

cues.en: Again, I'll show an example of this in a moment.
cues.zh: 稍後看例子。

cues.en: And finally we have batch size.
cues.zh: 最後，批次大小。

cues.en: This is just the number of sequences you enter into the model simultaneously to be processed.
cues.zh: 就是同時送進模型處理的序列數。

cues.en: Especially if you're training on a GPU, then the batch size can really help speed things up.
cues.zh: 尤其使用 GPU 訓練時，批次處理有助加快速度。

cues.en: All right, let's go through each one of these in more detail with an example.
cues.zh: 用例子，更詳細說明。

cues.en: I'm going to use this example text.
cues.zh: 使用這段文字：

cues.en: You can learn a lot of math with a bit of coding.
cues.zh: 只要寫一點程式，就能學到很多數學。

cues.en: That's my coin aphorism, and it's also the motto that drives my teaching.
cues.zh: 這是我自創的格言，也是推動我教學的座右銘。

cues.en: Okay, so let's focus on inputs and targets.
cues.zh: 先看輸入與目標。

cues.en: So here would be the inputs to the model during training.
cues.zh: 這是訓練時，模型的輸入，

cues.en: And here would be the targets.
cues.zh: 這是目標。

cues.en: So the targets are literally just the same sentence the same tokens.
cues.zh: 目標就是相同句子、相同 token，

cues.en: But the first token or the first word is dropped and the whole sentence is shifted.
cues.zh: 只是丟掉第一個 token，或者第一個單字，讓整句平移。

cues.en: So this means that when the model processes the token you it will try to predict the token can.
cues.zh: 所以，模型處理 you 時，要預測 can。

cues.en: And when it processes can, it's going to try to predict learn when it sees learn it will try to predict a and so on for all of these tokens, for all of these words.
cues.zh: 處理 can，要預測 learn；看到 learn，要預測 a，依此類推，對所有 token、所有單字都一樣。

cues.en: So the idea is that the model is always trying to predict the next token based on the current token, and also whatever preceding tokens it has access to.
cues.zh: 模型總是依目前 token，以及能存取的先前 token，預測下一個。

cues.en: now during training.
cues.zh: 訓練時，

cues.en: The loss is only calculated from the final token.
cues.zh: 損失只從最後一個 token 計算。

cues.en: So the model is always trying to predict the next token.
cues.zh: 模型一直在預測下一個 token，

cues.en: But for training we just take the loss from the final prediction.
cues.zh: 但訓練時，只取最後一次預測的損失。

cues.en: The reason for that is partly just convention, because that's just how most people do it.
cues.zh: 一部分只是慣例，因為大多數人都這樣做，

cues.en: So that's how other people do it.
cues.zh: 所以跟著做。

cues.en: But it's also partly based on the idea that the final token prediction has the most context.
cues.zh: 另一部分原因，是最後一個 token 的預測，有最多上下文。

cues.en: So the model has the most information it can leverage to predict this final token.
cues.zh: 模型有最多資訊，可以用來預測最後的 token。

cues.en: For example, if you only see the word you, it's really hard to guess what the next word is going to be.
cues.zh: 例如，只看到 you，很難猜下一個字。

cues.en: But if you see this entire sentence up to coding except for the period, it's a pretty good guess that what comes after this word coding is a period, or maybe a comma or whatever.
cues.zh: 但若看到整句，一直到 coding，只缺句點，就很容易猜 coding 之後是句點，或也許逗號之類。

cues.en: Anyway, so we're not really losing a lot of information, because each of these tokens can also be used as the final token.
cues.zh: 其實，沒有損失太多資訊，因為每個 token，也都可能被當成最後一個。

cues.en: Because token sequences are often segmented to be overlapping.
cues.zh: 因為 token 序列通常切成互相重疊的片段。

cues.en: I will get back to that point when I talk about stride.
cues.zh: 談步幅時，再回到這點。

cues.en: So next up is sequence length.
cues.zh: 接著，序列長度。

cues.en: This is also called context window or context length or something comparable.
cues.zh: 也叫上下文視窗、上下文長度，或類似名稱。

cues.en: So this parameter is I think it's pretty obvious what it means.
cues.zh: 這個參數的意思，應該很明顯。

cues.en: Here is a sequence of length 1212 words.
cues.zh: 這是長度 12，也就是 12 個單字的序列。

cues.en: Here is a sequence of length seven.
cues.zh: 這是長度 7 的序列。

cues.en: So the sequence length is literally just the number of tokens that you're giving to the model.
cues.zh: 序列長度，就是提供給模型的 token 數。

cues.en: Now in theory you want the sequence to be as long as possible, because the more context you can provide to the model, the better it can learn to predict the next token.
cues.zh: 理論上，越長越好，因為提供越多上下文，模型越能學會預測下一個 token。

cues.en: On the other hand, it's not trivially better just to have arbitrarily long sequences.
cues.zh: 但不是隨便加長，就必然更好。

cues.en: For example, let's say you're training text is the entirety of Wikipedia.
cues.zh: 例如，訓練文字是整個 Wikipedia。

cues.en: Now, it's certainly the case that 100 tokens would give more context than ten tokens.
cues.zh: 100 個 token，確實比十個提供更多上下文。

cues.en: But 100 million tokens spans probably a few thousand, maybe a few hundred thousand different Wikipedia pages.
cues.zh: 但一億個 token，可能橫跨幾千，甚至幾十萬個不同頁面。

cues.en: So it's not really clear that having such a ludicrously high sequence length is beneficial.
cues.zh: 這麼誇張的序列長度，是否有益，就不清楚了。

cues.en: But even if we think about sequence lengths in the range of a few hundreds to a few thousands, then
cues.zh: 即使只考慮數百到數千的範圍，

cues.en: the primary disadvantage of longer sequences is increased computational demands.
cues.zh: 較長序列的主要缺點，也是計算需求增加。

cues.en: In fact, in the code for the rest of this section, I'm going to use sequence lengths of either 8 or 6.
cues.zh: 這一章後面的程式，其實只用長度 8 或 6。

cues.en: Now that is way, way, way too short for any real meaningful training of a real embeddings matrix.
cues.zh: 對真正有意義的嵌入矩陣訓練，這實在短得太多。

cues.en: But having a short sequence length just makes the computation time more feasible.
cues.zh: 但短序列，能讓計算時間更可行。

cues.en: So we just have to wait seconds or maybe a few minutes for training time instead of hours or days each time we want to train the model.
cues.zh: 每次訓練只要等幾秒或幾分鐘，而不是幾小時或幾天。

cues.en: Okay, next up is stride.
cues.zh: 接著是步幅，

cues.en: So this is also sometimes called skip.
cues.zh: 有時也叫 skip。

cues.en: The idea is that we want to train using token sequences that are cut out of a very long text, like a book or a Wikipedia page or a scientific article.
cues.zh: 構想是，從書籍、Wikipedia 頁面或科學文章這類長文字，切出 token 序列訓練。

cues.en: And we also want to maximize our training data and calculate the loss based on lots of tokens, not
cues.zh: 也希望盡量利用訓練資料，讓損失根據許多 token 計算，

cues.en: just the ones that just so happened to be at the end of a sequence.
cues.zh: 而不是只根據剛好位在序列末尾的那些。

cues.en: Okay, so imagine this sentence.
cues.zh: 想像這個句子。

cues.en: Here is the full text.
cues.zh: 這是完整文字，

cues.en: Obviously in practice it's way, way longer.
cues.zh: 實務上當然長得多，

cues.en: But let's just work with this.
cues.zh: 但先用這個。

cues.en: This is the full text.
cues.zh: 這就是全文。

cues.en: So now let's say we are training with a sequence length of six.
cues.zh: 假設序列長度為 6，

cues.en: So we're going to input six tokens into the model at a time.
cues.zh: 一次送入模型六個 token。

cues.en: If we have a stride of one, then the first two sentences or the first two token sequences that we enter
cues.zh: 步幅為 1 時，最初兩個句子，或者說兩個 token 序列，

cues.en: into the model are, you can learn a lot of that would be sequence one, and the second sequence would be can learn a lot of math.
cues.zh: 第一個是 you can learn a lot of，第二個則是 can learn a lot of math。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So the idea is that the losses that the model uses now come from predicting of and also from predicting math.
cues.zh: 構想是，模型的損失，會來自預測 of，以及預測 math。

cues.en: So we're really getting a lot of training data out of this one sentence here.
cues.zh: 所以，從這一句，就取得很多訓練資料。

cues.en: But there are two issues with having a stride of one.
cues.zh: 但步幅 1，有兩個問題。

cues.en: One issue is just practical.
cues.zh: 一個是實務問題，

cues.en: The computation time increases a lot because the text is broken down into so many different sequences.
cues.zh: 文字拆成太多序列，計算時間大幅增加。

cues.en: But a second issue is that these two sentences are extremely highly correlated with each other.
cues.zh: 另一個，是兩個句子高度相關，

cues.en: They are nearly identical, except for one word in the beginning and one word at the end.
cues.zh: 幾乎相同，只有開頭與結尾各差一個字。

cues.en: And of course, this is a very simple example with a small sequence.
cues.zh: 當然，這是短序列的簡單例子。

cues.en: If you have a larger sequence length, then the correlation would be really, really high.
cues.zh: 序列更長，相關就更高。

cues.en: So it would be ideal if each of the inputs we provide to the model during training were independent of each other.
cues.zh: 理想上，訓練時給模型的各輸入，應彼此獨立。

cues.en: So the balance here is to set the stride to be a little bit higher.
cues.zh: 折衷做法，是把步幅設大一點。

cues.en: So for example here is a stride of three.
cues.zh: 例如，這裡步幅為 3。

cues.en: Now notice that the first input is still the first six tokens of this sentence or the first six words of this text.
cues.zh: 注意，第一個輸入，仍是原句最前面六個 token，也就是六個字。

cues.en: But the second the second sequence here actually starts three tokens later.
cues.zh: 第二個序列，則從後面第三個 token 的位置開始移動。

cues.en: So this is finding a balance between increasing the amount of training data and allowing the loss calculation
cues.zh: 也就是在增加訓練資料，讓損失根據更多 token 預測計算，

cues.en: to be based on more token predictions, and allowing a little bit of overlap or a little bit of correlation between successive sequences.
cues.zh: 以及允許相鄰序列有些重疊、相關之間，取得平衡。

cues.en: But so even though these two are a bit correlated, it's certainly a lot less compared to with a stride of one.
cues.zh: 雖然兩者仍有點相關，但比步幅 1 少得多。

cues.en: Okay, so that is the stride parameter.
cues.zh: 這就是步幅參數。

cues.en: The batch size is just the number of sequences that you give to the model to process at the same time.
cues.zh: 批次大小，就是同時讓模型處理的序列數。

cues.en: In part, this is really just about increasing computational efficiency by leveraging the parallel processing offered by GPUs.
cues.zh: 一部分，是利用 GPU 的平行處理，提高計算效率。

cues.en: But having larger batches does mean that the losses get averaged together, which can smooth out the learning trajectory a little bit, and therefore is a form of regularization.
cues.zh: 較大批次也讓損失取平均，使學習軌跡稍微平滑，因此也是一種正規化。

cues.en: So here you see a batch size of one, because there's only one token sequence that we are presenting to the model.
cues.zh: 這是批次大小 1，因為只給模型一個 token 序列。

cues.en: And this would be an example of a batch size of three where we give the model three input sequences at the same time.
cues.zh: 這是批次大小 3，同時給模型三個輸入序列。

cues.en: Of course we're also giving the corresponding target sequences.
cues.zh: 當然，也給對應的目標序列，

cues.en: I'm just not illustrating that here.
cues.zh: 只是這裡沒有畫出。

cues.en: Okay, so these are the main parameters and terms to know for training an embedding matrix.
cues.zh: 這些就是訓練嵌入矩陣，主要需要知道的參數與術語。

cues.en: Now one thing I want to mention before telling you about what you'll see in Python is that I've been
cues.zh: 說明 Python 內容前，還想提一點：這裡用

cues.en: showing letters and words here for convenience, so it's easier for you to interpret, but in practice, we're not actually giving the model words.
cues.zh: 字母與單字，只是為了方便理解；實務上，不是真的給模型單字，

cues.en: We're giving the model integer token IDs that were based on the tokenizer.
cues.zh: 而是 tokenizer 產生的整數 token ID。

cues.en: Okay, so here is what you are going to see in Python.
cues.zh: 這是在 Python 會看到的內容。

cues.en: We are going to import some text, split it into words and create a vocab from all the unique words.
cues.zh: 匯入文字、拆成單字，再用所有不重複單字建立詞彙表。

cues.en: We'll print this out to see that there are 30,000 words and 4500 unique words in the vocab.
cues.zh: 印出可看到，全文約 3 萬字，詞彙表約 4,500 個不重複單字。

cues.en: And here I've just printed out the first ten of the vocab words.
cues.zh: 這裡只印出詞彙表前十個字。

cues.en: Next we will create input and target lists of integers or token IDs.
cues.zh: 接著，建立輸入與目標的整數串列，也就是 token ID。

cues.en: Now notice that the targets here are just shifted versions of the inputs.
cues.zh: 注意，目標只是輸入平移後的版本。

cues.en: So the model sees input 2416 whatever word that happens to correspond to.
cues.zh: 模型看到輸入 2416，不論它對應什麼字，

cues.en: And its goal is to predict or to output 131.
cues.zh: 目標是預測、輸出 131。

cues.en: And then at the next token the model sees the token 131.
cues.zh: 下一個 token，模型看到 131，

cues.en: And its goal is to output 2172 and so on.
cues.zh: 目標則是輸出 2172，依此類推。

cues.en: You can also see that these sequences, these lists are each one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight.
cues.zh: 也能數出，這些串列各有一、二、三、四、五、六、七、八個。

cues.en: So here I'm using a sequence length of eight.
cues.zh: 所以，這裡序列長度為 8。

cues.en: So the model always tries to predict the following token.
cues.zh: 模型一直試著預測下一個 token。

cues.en: These two are the first sentence or the first sequence.
cues.zh: 這兩列是第一個句子，或者說序列，

cues.en: And these two rows here correspond to the second sequence.
cues.zh: 下面兩列，則是第二個序列。

cues.en: So question for you based on what you see on this slide, What is the stride parameter that I set?
cues.zh: 問你，依照這張投影片，步幅設為多少？

cues.en: Feel free to pause the video if you need a moment to think about it.
cues.zh: 如果需要思考，可以暫停。

cues.en: So the answer is that the stride parameter is two.
cues.zh: 答案是 2。

cues.en: Notice that in the second sequence, the first input in the sequence is 2172, which is the third item in the first sequence, which means.
cues.zh: 第二序列的第一個輸入 2172，是第一序列的第三個項目，代表，

cues.en: Here we start with 2416.
cues.zh: 這裡從 2416 開始，

cues.en: And then the next sequence skips two tokens, and then we start there on the second token.
cues.zh: 下一序列跳過兩個 token，再從那個位置開始。

cues.en: In other words, this second sequence is literally just the first sequence, but starting two tokens later.
cues.zh: 換句話說，第二序列就是第一序列，往後移兩個 token。

cues.en: And of course we get two new tokens in here.
cues.zh: 當然，這裡也多兩個新 token。

cues.en: So the entire text is around 30,000 tokens long.
cues.zh: 整段文字約 3 萬個 token，

cues.en: And so yeah, this is there's a lot more room to keep adding more and more sequences here.
cues.zh: 所以，還有很多空間，繼續加入更多序列。

cues.en: Once we have the data organized we are going to create a data loader.
cues.zh: 整理好資料，就建立 DataLoader，

cues.en: So a special data type used for PyTorch called a data loader.
cues.zh: 也就是 PyTorch 使用的特殊資料型別。

cues.en: And first we will define a dataset class so that you see here.
cues.zh: 先定義 Dataset 類別，就是這裡。

cues.en: Here's a screenshot of the code.
cues.zh: 這是程式截圖。

cues.en: I'll discuss all of these lines in more detail when I switch to Python.
cues.zh: 切換到 Python 時，會更詳細解釋每行。

cues.en: But basically what you see is that we have a class.
cues.zh: 基本上，這是一個類別。

cues.en: We initialize inputs and targets, and the lookup table, which is the same Python dictionary that we've now created several times.
cues.zh: 初始化輸入、目標，以及查找表，也就是已建立好幾次的 Python 字典。

cues.en: It's what we're using for an encoder.
cues.zh: 它用來當編碼器。

cues.en: And then in this for loop over here we are generating sequences for the inputs and the targets.
cues.zh: 接著，在這個 for 迴圈，產生輸入與目標序列。

cues.en: And you can also see that I'm transforming these into PyTorch tensors.
